newsitem.title: YUGOSLAVIA: Serbia grants 840 mln DM credits to boost exports.
newsitem.headline: Serbia grants 840 mln DM credits to boost exports.

text.p: The Serbian Development Fund has so far granted 840 million German marks ($450 million) in favourable loans to boost export industries, the Belgrade daily Privredni pregled (Economic Review) reported on Tuesday.

Serbia clinched a strategic deal in early June, in a boost for the ruling Socialists, to sell 49 percent of Telekom Srbija to the Greek and Italian companies OTE and Stet for 1.568 billion marks. The Fund is the only recepient of the money raised from the sale. Eighty percent was paid into the Fund's account immediately after the deal was made and the rest is to be paid next January.

The government, facing a chronic shortage of cash to revive idle industries after 1992-96 war-related U.N. sanctions, said it would support export industries to boost production, utilisation of factory capacities and sales abroad.
It said it would extend three to six months hard currency credits at an annual interest rate of four percent only for economically viable programmes.

Out of the 840 million marks of credits granted to date, 246 million marks were extended for export-oriented production in companies from various industry branches which employ over 100,000 people. The government expects increased capacity utilisation and re-employment of 15,000 workers now on compulsory leave.

The Fund invested 75 million marks in a 1997 wheat crop buy-up, 54 million marks for cattle breeding, 29 million for fruit exports and 10 million for imports of wool and cotton. Some 100 million marks was earmarked for production of agricultural machinery which includes 26 companies with 300 subcontractors.

Another 160 million marks was allocated for development of the road network, 100 million for modernisation of the rail system, 30 million for revitalisation of power industry Elektroprivreda Srbije and 30 million for gasification of Serbia.

Serbian Privatisation Minister Milan Beko said the credits would secure a rise in utilisation both of capacities and labour and provide the means for companies to return to the international market. Industry Minister Zivota Cosic said besides the production and exports boost and rise in real wages, credits would also contribute to the quicker collection of budget revenues.
But local analysts expressed fear the cash injections would not be enough to secure steady development due to burgeoning company losses, outdated technology and social tensions.
Economists say the country needs some $2 billion annually for the next five years to keep its economy going.
"We have to be realistic, some of the companies will not be able to meet their liabilities on time" one analyst said.

Analysts also warned that the lion's share of the funds would be used for late payouts to workers and farmers, pensioners, teachers, doctors and nurses to calm growing social unrest ahead of coming elections.
According to media reports, only few companies from the opposition-run Serbian towns, received the Fund's loans.
Serbia's presidental and parliamentary elections are set for September 21. -- Belgrade newsroom, 381 11 311 4275
